tasks.short: Run training sessions with role play, toolbox talks, group exercises, videos and short lectures on three sites.

steps.what: Choose session format and exercises for the group and site

loop.input: course outline, target group, site incident summaries without names
loop.output: session plan with two or three role-play or case scenarios
loop.check: L&D specialist reads and edits; safety scenarios go to the site safety lead
loop.stop: one draft plus at most two revisions on request; fallback is the existing plan template
loop.why_not_simpler: Realistic scenarios have to be written from free-text incident notes and local practice; a template cannot do that.

steps.what: Prepare slides, role-play scripts, videos and exercise cards
Deliver the session in person, lead role play and discussion
Book rooms, invite attendees, send reminders
Collect participant reactions and send follow-up material

tasks.design: Studytube AI Authoring and Microsoft 365 Copilot draft session plans, scenarios and slides from existing outlines; the specialist edits and the safety lead signs safety content. Studytube sessions and Outlook handle booking, reminders and the follow-up survey. Delivery stays in person; a disclosed AI practice partner lets team leads rehearse feedback conversations between sessions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing good scenarios and exercises took expert time and could not be templated; booking ran through mail because nobody set up Studytube session management.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube AI Authoring and Copilot draft outlines, scripts and questions from a title or document, and a model can play a counterpart in a practice conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, handling resistance on the warehouse floor and judging practical skill stay human; drafted scenarios still need local facts checked.
tasks.human_edge: Leading a group of shift workers in person, adapting on the spot, and judging whether people can actually do the task.

ambition.what: A disclosed AI feedback-practice partner for shift leaders, using the Situation-Behavior-Impact rubric, between classroom sessions.

tasks.altitude: About half of preparation time comes back and goes into more floor sessions and coaching. The specialist decides which sessions get a practice follow-up.

reach.learn: Which feedback situations shift leaders struggle with, to build practice scenarios from them.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded file; authors edit.
Workday's agent drafting manager feedback against the SBI rubric raised users' quality 16 points against 7 for non-users.
An AI tutor must disclose it is AI; inferring learners' emotions from a webcam is banned.
Assistance helped novices most (34% more resolutions per hour).

assumptions: Noordhaven has the Studytube AI Authoring module or can license it.
Microsoft 365 Copilot or an approved model is available under the company's data agreement.
Most delivery is classroom and toolbox talks on site.
unknowns: Whether Studytube session management is already in use for classroom bookings.
How many shift leaders would use a practice tool and in which language.
Whether the works council sees the practice tool as monitoring under WOR 27(1)(l).
research_questions: Does a pilot group of 15 shift leaders who practise with the AI partner write better SBI feedback after six weeks than a control group?
How many preparation hours per session does Studytube AI Authoring save on three real Noordhaven courses?
Do warehouse staff rate AI-drafted scenarios as realistic as hand-written ones?

tasks.short: Write and update manuals, handouts, slides and e-learning from work instructions and safety rules.

steps.what: Gather work instructions, SOPs and expert input from sites
Draft handouts, slides, e-learning and quiz questions
Simplify reading level and translate for flex workers

loop.input: approved Dutch course draft and a glossary of fixed safety terms
loop.output: plain-language Dutch, English and Polish versions
loop.check: readability score per section, glossary terms must match exactly, a native-speaking site colleague spot-checks safety parts
loop.stop: two rewrite passes per section; sections still failing go to manual translation
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting to a lower reading level and translating free text needs a language model; machine translation alone breaks fixed safety terms.

steps.what: Subject expert and safety lead review and sign off
Publish in Studytube and SharePoint, keep versions

tasks.design: A SharePoint library holds approved work instructions; Studytube AI Authoring turns them into course drafts and quizzes, and a bounded translation step with a fixed safety glossary produces plain Dutch, English and Polish versions. A Power Automate flow routes drafts to the safety lead for sign-off, then publishes to Studytube and flags courses whose source instruction changed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drafting and translating material was skilled writing work with no tool that could produce a usable first version from a PDF.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube AI Authoring drafts from uploaded files, and models now rewrite and translate text well enough to edit instead of write.
tasks.still_hard: Getting correct, current work instructions from sites, and expert time for safety review; errors in safety content can hurt people.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what workers really need to know, checking facts against how the job is done on the floor, and owning sign-off on safety content with the safety lead.

ambition.what: Flex workers from the three agencies get induction and safety handouts in their own language before their first shift.

tasks.altitude: Writing time drops to editing; the specialist spends more time on site checking that material matches practice. They own the glossary and the source-to-course link.

reach.task: Preparing onboarding packs for new hires
reach.learn: Which documents new starters and flex workers actually receive and when.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts courses from PDF, PPT or SCORM; vendor claims minutes per course.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing.
Workers spend much of their AI time fixing output, so review time must be counted.
VCA and forklift certification is done by outside bodies; material only prepares learners.

assumptions: A large share of flex workers do not read Dutch well; Polish is a main language.
Work instructions exist as documents on SharePoint or with site leads.
A safety lead per site can sign off safety content.
unknowns: Which languages flex workers speak, by site and season.
How current and complete the work instructions are.
Whether the safety leads have time for faster review cycles.
research_questions: How long does it take to turn three existing work instructions into approved Studytube courses with AI Authoring against today?
How many errors does the safety lead find in AI drafts and translations, and of what kind?
Do flex workers pass the induction quiz more often with material in their own language?

tasks.short: Plan, schedule and enrol staff in mandatory and skills training, mostly certificates for shift staff.

steps.what: Find who needs training: expiring certificates, new hires, manager requests
Match each need to a course or programme

loop.input: free-text manager requests and the course catalogue
loop.output: suggested course per request with a one-line reason
loop.check: specialist accepts or changes each suggestion; mandatory certificates follow fixed rules, not the model
loop.stop: one suggestion per request; no match goes to the specialist
loop.why_not_simpler: Manager requests are free text; certificate needs are handled by rules and need no model.

steps.what: Schedule sessions around shift rosters and book external trainers
Enrol workers, inform them and their team leads
Chase no-shows and rebook before certificates lapse

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform joins Studytube certificate expiry dates, AFAS employees and shift rosters, and agency flex worker orders, and proposes session dates per site 60 days before a lapse. The specialist approves the proposal and trainer bookings; Studytube then enrols people, Teams notifies team leads, and no-shows are rebooked automatically with an escalation list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates, rosters and flex orders sat in separate systems, tied together by an Excel sheet and mail; nobody had time to build and maintain the link.
tasks.enabler_now: Studytube and AFAS expose data by API or export, and AI coding makes a small join-and-schedule job a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Rosters change late, external trainers have limited dates, and flex worker data from agency portals may be thin or late.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with site managers when people can leave the floor, choosing trainers, and handling the person who keeps missing training.

ambition.what: Flex workers' forklift and VCA status checked against the agency order before their first shift.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops building the monthly certificate sheet and approves schedules instead. They gain the right to block a shift booking for someone without a valid certificate, agreed with site managers.

reach.task: Handling flex worker orders from agency portals
reach.learn: Which certificate data agencies supply with an order and how late.

evidence.claim: Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling fit deterministic software using Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters.
Microsoft Learning agent suggests skill gaps and pathways, with HR still guiding role moves.
Training policy and personal data processing need works council consent.

assumptions: Shift rosters are in AFAS or exportable from a planning tool.
Mandatory certificates are recorded in Studytube with expiry dates.
Agency portals offer an export of orders with worker names.
unknowns: Where shift rosters are kept and how far ahead they are fixed.
Whether agencies share flex workers' certificate data and under which contract terms.
How many certificates lapse today before renewal.
research_questions: How many shift workers worked with an expired forklift or VCA certificate in the last year?
Can the three agency portals deliver worker and certificate data before the first shift?
Does a 60-day proposal cut no-shows and last-minute rebookings in a three-month trial at one site?

tasks.short: Record attendance, collect evaluations and report on whether training works.

steps.what: Export completions, merge with headcount in Excel
Type paper sign-in sheets into Studytube
Read evaluation comments and summarise themes

loop.input: anonymised free-text comments per course, groups of five or more
loop.output: themes with counts and example quotes
loop.check: specialist reads a sample against themes; no output below five respondents; no names
loop.stop: one pass per course per quarter; unclassified comments listed raw
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments are free text in several languages; keyword rules miss most themes.

steps.what: Compare training with onboarding, 90-day retention and certification outcomes
Write quarterly report for HR director and site managers

tasks.design: Studytube session check-in by QR code replaces paper lists, and the nightly AFAS extract plus a Studytube feed land in a Power BI L&D page showing week-one onboarding, first-shift certification and 90-day retention by course and site. A bounded model step clusters anonymised comments at group level only, and the quarterly report is generated from the dashboard for the specialist to edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Studytube data was not in the Power BI extract, attendance was on paper, and free-text comments took too long to read.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already feeds Power BI nightly, adding a Studytube source is small, and models cluster short comments reliably enough for review.
tasks.still_hard: Showing that a course caused better retention; small groups, seasonal flex swings and no baseline make cause hard to prove.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing measures with managers before a course starts and judging what the numbers mean for the programme.

ambition.what: Keep, fix or stop each course decided quarterly on outcome data instead of once a year on attendance.

tasks.altitude: No more monthly Excel merges; the specialist sets baselines with managers and decides course changes. Data stays at group level and outside appraisals.

reach.task: Maintaining the Power BI HR dashboards on the AFAS extract
reach.learn: How retention and onboarding measures are defined so L&D uses the same ones.

evidence.claim: MHR agrees measures with the manager first, collects at six weeks and six months, and uses AI to cluster comments, not to decide.
No opened source shows a course cutting time-to-skill; Workday advises baselines before launch.
From 2 December 2027, AI using learning data to evaluate workers is high-risk under Annex III 4(b).
Monitoring-capable tools need works council consent under WOR 27(1)(l).

assumptions: The people analyst can add a Studytube source to the Power BI model.
Studytube offers QR or self check-in for classroom sessions.
Comment analysis stays at group level and never feeds appraisal.
unknowns: Whether Studytube data can be exported by API under the current contract.
Which outcome measures the HR director and site managers will accept.
Whether the works council agrees to linking training records to retention data.
research_questions: Does the Power BI page show a link between week-one onboarding completion and 90-day retention per site?
Do model comment themes match a specialist's hand coding on 200 comments?
Will the works council consent to group-level reporting with a minimum group size of five?

role.altitude: The two specialists move from making courses and Excel registers to owning the competence record for 1,200 staff and flex workers, the Article 4 AI literacy file, and the decision to keep or stop courses on outcome data.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: shared outcome measures in Power BI
HR Administrator: flex worker onboarding and agency data
HR Business Partner: manager coaching and feedback practice
skills_to_grow: Editing and checking AI-drafted material against floor practice
Data literacy in Power BI and basic data joins
Setting baselines and outcome measures with managers
EU AI Act Art. 4 and Art. 50 and works council procedure
role.ambitious_version: Every shift worker, including flex staff, starts with valid certificates and induction in their own language, and L&D reports quarterly on how training moves week-one onboarding and 90-day retention.
